03_cancel_after_cancel_status_guard.plan.title: SKIP_STEP / workflow guard: cancel endpoint may accept a second request after the order already reached the terminal 'canceled' state
03_cancel_after_cancel_status_guard.plan.unsupported_reason: The hypothesis is that the server should reject (e.g. 4xx, or a no-op response with orderStatus unchanged) a second POST /api/order/cancel once order.orderStatus is already 'canceled' and order.availableActions.cancelOrder is already false — a workflow-state/status-equality guard, not a numeric amount comparison. sum_lte cannot express 'the second call must be rejected' or 'orderStatus must remain exactly canceled without re-processing'. The resulting financial impact of this same missing guard, if any, is separately covered by the amount_bound double-cancel scenario (01_double_cancel_amount_bound.plan.json).

04_duplicate_history_entry_integrity.pla.title: DATA_TAMPER / integrity: repeated cancel calls may append duplicate 'order_canceled' ledger entries to order history
04_duplicate_history_entry_integrity.pla.unsupported_reason: The hypothesis is that order.history should contain exactly one 'order_canceled' entry regardless of how many times cancel is called (an array-length/uniqueness check on the event ledger), not a numeric sum comparison. sum_lte only expresses 'sum of numeric fields <= a numeric limit' and cannot count array entries or check for duplicate event types. This requires a count/uniqueness predicate not currently supported by the plan schema.

05_repeated_cancel_authorization_enforce.title: FORCED_BROWSING / authorization enforcement: server may not enforce its own advertised availableActions.cancelOrder=false flag
05_repeated_cancel_authorization_enforce.unsupported_reason: The hypothesis is that once GET /api/order reports availableActions.cancelOrder=false, the server must itself enforce that flag and refuse a direct POST /api/order/cancel call reaching it via forced browsing (i.e. bypassing the client-side disabled/hidden button) — an authorization/enforcement claim about whether the client-only flag is also checked server-side, not a numeric sum comparison. sum_lte cannot express 'the server must reject a call that its own response marked as unavailable.' The financial consequence of this same gap, if the call is accepted, is covered separately by the amount_bound double-cancel scenario (01_double_cancel_amount_bound.plan.json).
